title: Mind the Gap: The Non-Fundamental Role of Earnings Days
one_line: The part of an earnings-day return not explained by the earnings surprise (Return-Earnings Gap) is largely non-fundamental: it reverses — about 21% within a year and ~54% within three years — and distorts later analyst forecasts and anomaly returns.

findings.statement: REG long-short earns 10.4% on the announcement day (DGTW-adjusted).
Reversal 9.9% of the day-t move within 21 days, 21.4% at 1 year, 54.5% at 3 years.

why.pattern: Earnings days amplify non-fundamental moves as well as correcting mispricing.

reported_results.headline: The part of an earnings-day return not explained by the earnings surprise (Return-Earnings Gap) is largely non-fundamental: it reverses — about 21% within a year and ~54% within three years — and distorts later analyst forecasts and anomaly returns.

tradable_edge: Stock-level; slow reversal, not tradable on ES/NQ.
data_fit: Single-stock study — not testable on our ES/NQ data.
caveats: Read by Claude in a chat session (manual run 5, 2026-11-10), not by the weekly pipeline.
